$schemaNote: Machine-readable external/human gate state consumed by tooling/release/Invoke-ReleaseGateCheck.ps1. Every gate here is BLOCKED or EXTERNAL by definition until an owner outside this repository-editing lane closes it and records evidence. Do not set status to CLOSED/GREEN from within an automated script or an agent lane -- it must be updated by hand by the accountable human owner with an evidence reference. EVERY gate MUST carry BOTH 'releaseScope' and 'conditionalReleaseScope' as EXPLICIT JSON ARRAYS (never omitted, never null, never a bare string) -- the release-gate script fails the WHOLE evaluation closed on a missing/null/non-array value or an invalid/duplicate token rather than silently treating it as an empty scope (DW-W1-R1 P0-1). 'releaseScope' names the release target(s) this gate HARD-blocks (a base release cannot be READY for that target while the gate is non-CLOSED). 'conditionalReleaseScope' names release target(s) where this gate is a real but CONDITIONAL/feature-scoped dependency (maps to a FABLE PARTIAL cell) -- it is surfaced separately (see the script's CONDITIONAL_GATES_PENDING output) but never counted as a hard blocker of that target's BASE release. A target absent from both arrays is unaffected by this gate entirely (maps to a FABLE NO cell). Both arrays being empty ('releaseScope': [], 'conditionalReleaseScope': []) means the gate currently blocks no release target at all, hard or conditional (e.g. TELEMETRY_ACTIVATION_OWNER_SIGNOFF, which gates ACTIVATING telemetry rather than any release capability, and so can never legitimately close yet must never falsely block a release either). Valid release targets (see docs/supervision/PCA_FABLE_EXTERNAL_GATE_RELEASE_SCOPE.csv, the authoritative per-gate x per-target YES/PARTIAL/NO scoping answer key -- YES maps to releaseScope, PARTIAL maps to conditionalReleaseScope, NO maps to neither): PUBLIC_A, AUTH_B, PARENT_C, ANDROID_D, IOS_FUTURE, BILLING_FUTURE. tooling/release/ValidateFableScopeParity.mjs performs a full, non-sampled reconciliation of every row in that CSV against this file plus the two source-derived signals (PRODUCTION_CRYPTO_SUITE, REAL_UAT) and must be re-run after any edit here.

gates.description: Deployed log/metrics pipeline configuration (reverse proxy / container log shipping) for the relay's routing-metadata-only logging surface. Source proof is strong (type-level exclusion of plaintext fields, Fastify logger disabled, noPayloadLoggingHttp.test.mjs regression, zero stray console/log call sites); the remaining gap is infra-level deployment configuration not present in this repository beyond a plain Dockerfile.

Deployed production TLS-termination configuration (reverse proxy / load balancer) is an infrastructure concern outside this repository. Confirmed via direct repo-wide search that no TLS termination is implemented or claimed in-repo, so this requirement is correctly NOT_APPLICABLE to source with the deployment step tracked as an external gate. Any HTTPS publication, on any release target, needs TLS termination configured -- the one gate here that is genuinely scoped to every target including PUBLIC_A.

Formal product/privacy-owner sign-off required before ever activating optional telemetry. Consent module (backend/src/telemetry/consent.ts) defaults off, has an explicit distinct grant/revoke, enforces an allowlisted aggregate-only event shape, and noTelemetryEndpoint.test.mjs proves zero ingestion routes exist anywhere in the product; building ingestion infrastructure ahead of sign-off would violate PCA-NFR-014/PRIV-002 rather than satisfy it. This gate governs ACTIVATING telemetry, not any release capability -- it can never legitimately close before a release and must never be allowed to block one either, so its releaseScope is intentionally empty (see docs/supervision/PCA_FABLE_EXTERNAL_GATE_RELEASE_SCOPE.csv: 'a permanent false blocker' prior to this fix).

Inbound delivery to the four public addresses (contact, security-disclosure, etc.) has been verified, but public Send-As / reply identity remains NOT_READY -- the product cannot yet reply to the public from its own identity. A published contact/security-disclosure surface that cannot reply from its own identity is a genuine Release A (PUBLIC_A) hard blocker. It also touches AUTH_B's shared email sending / domain-authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) path, but per docs/supervision/PCA_FABLE_EXTERNAL_GATE_RELEASE_SCOPE.csv that is a PARTIAL/conditional dependency for AUTH_B, not a hard base-release blocker -- AUTH_B's own hard sender/domain-authentication requirement is tracked under PRODUCTION_EMAIL_DELIVERY (do not double-count it here as a hard AUTH_B blocker). Do not expose the private forwarding mailbox in any artifact. Was previously absent from this register entirely. See docs/supervision/PCA_FABLE_OPEN_ACTION_REGISTER.csv FABLE-A064 and docs/release_readiness/reports (RELEASE_A_CONTACT_CHANNEL_VERIFICATION.md referenced there).

PCA-DW-W2/W2-R1 built a complete production-grade email architecture in backend/src/email (EmailService, an encrypted-at-rest durable outbox, bounded retry/dead-letter, SMTP + Microsoft Graph provider adapters, keyed idempotency, provider timeouts, TLS enforcement, redacted error metadata) -- this gate is NOT about missing code. With no PCA_EMAIL_PROVIDER configured, the architecture correctly fails closed to a RejectingEmailProviderAdapter (never a silent fake-success), so markVerified still has no real production email path and no parent can log in without one; this remains the AUTH_B blocker and must not be filed under PAYMENT_PROVIDER_SELECTION. Requires: an approved real provider; production credentials configured; verification-email delivery proven externally; reset-email delivery proven externally; sender identity and domain authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) verified; and no test-sandbox adapter active in production. PUBLIC_A does not need this (no account system on the public site). ANDROID_D/IOS_FUTURE are a PARTIAL/conditional dependency only (where enrollment invitations travel by email) -- NOT a hard blocker of their base release, per docs/supervision/PCA_FABLE_EXTERNAL_GATE_RELEASE_SCOPE.csv. See docs/supervision/PCA_FABLE_OPEN_ACTION_REGISTER.csv FABLE-A006/FABLE-A061 and docs/supervision/PCA_DYNAMIC_WORKFLOW_W2_CLOSURE.md for the architecture's own evidence.
